Build a dimoose key from a table of leads

Source: R/keys.R
keyFromLeads.Rd

The common constructor behind sharkKey(), arachnidaKey(), vibrioKey() and phylotreeKey(): takes one row per lead and returns a dimoose object.

Usage

keyFromLeads(leads, desc = NA, meta = NULL, taxa = NULL, features = NULL)

Arguments

leads

Data frame with columns Statement (couplet), Choice, Character (the lead's text), Next (next couplet, or "-" if the lead ends in a result) and Taxon (the result, for terminal leads). Optional columns Label, Image, ImageLink and TaxonUrl are used by exportWizard(); any others are kept.

desc

Title or description of the key.

meta

Key/value data frame of metadata (e.g. citation).

taxa

Data frame of results with submitted_name and matched_name; by default every taxon matches itself.

features

Optional featureTable() for keys a machine can follow (the leads then also carry Feature, Test and Threshold).

Value

A dimoose object.

Examples

leads <- data.frame(
  Statement = c("1", "1", "2", "2"), Choice = c("a", "b", "a", "b"),
  Character = c("Wings present", "Wings absent", "Two wings", "Four wings"),
  Next = c("2", "-", "-", "-"), Taxon = c("", "Apterygota", "Diptera", "Other")
)
k <- keyFromLeads(leads, "A tiny key")
k
#> <dimoose key> A tiny key
#>   2 couplets, 4 leads, 3 taxa, up to 2 steps deep
k$toNewick()
#> [1] "((Diptera,Other)2,Apterygota)1;"
